area: MCP servers: scopes, approval, allow/deny lists, mcp__ permission rules, tool search, managed MCP, hooks

facts.behavior: Local (default) is 'Current project only', private, stored in ~/.claude.json. Project is shared via version control in .mcp.json at project root. User is all your projects, stored in ~/.claude.json. Precedence: local, project, user, plugin servers, claude.ai connectors. 'The entire server entry from that source is used; fields are not merged across scopes.' Duplicates match by name across the three scopes; plugins and connectors match by endpoint.
facts.limits: Not a settings.json key; MCP server definitions live in ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json, not in the settings precedence stack. A managedMcpServers entry (v2.1.259+) outranks all of these.

facts.behavior: Supports ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} in command, args, env, url, headers. Unset var without default: config still loads, warning in claude mcp list, unexpanded text used as-is.
facts.limits: Credential-like names (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, HTTPS_PROXY, NPM_TOKEN) read as empty in remote url and headers even if set, and a :-default is ignored. A name like API_KEY expands normally.

facts.behavior: 'Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using project-scoped servers from .mcp.json files.' Unapproved shows '⏸ Pending approval' and is not connected. claude mcp reset-project-choices clears approvals/rejections.
facts.limits: In claude -p, Agent SDK, and cloud sessions outside a project Claude Code 'can't show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking' (approved or not; claude mcp list still reports pending). Also skipped in bypassPermissions mode when skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt is set in user or managed settings. Not a hook or permission-rule surface.

facts.behavior: Settings keys that pre-approve .mcp.json servers. 'A cloned repository can't approve its own servers': committed in the project's .claude/settings.json they are ignored in an untrusted folder. They still apply from user ~/.claude/settings.json, managed settings, and --settings. Untracked .claude/settings.local.json approvals apply only in a trusted folder.
facts.limits: Approval only; not a restriction. Unrelated to disabledMcpServers/enabledMcpServers (the /mcp toggles).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (project server approvals and workspace trust)

facts.behavior: 'A disabledMcpjsonServers entry in any settings file still rejects the server' and 'blocks it in every permission mode'; rejects a .mcp.json server by name in every session type, including -p/SDK. Status: '✘ Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers in settings)'.
facts.limits: Matches by name only, and only .mcp.json servers (not user/local scope, plugins, or connectors). Name is user-assigned, so it is not a robust identity control.

facts.feature: Other ways to keep project MCP servers out
facts.behavior: --setting-sources user (or SDK settingSources without project) reads neither project settings nor .mcp.json; --bare reads no hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins or .mcp.json servers from the project; --strict-mcp-config uses only servers from --mcp-config (skipping the prompt needs v2.1.246+).
facts.limits: --bare still applies the project's env block and helpers like awsAuthRefresh. --strict-mcp-config with managed-mcp.json deployed makes Claude Code exit at startup. Per-session flags, not persistent policy.

facts.behavior: 'To match every tool from an MCP server, write mcp__<server>__*. To match one tool, write its full name, mcp__<server>__<tool>.' mcp__puppeteer (bare server) also matches all its tools. Characters like . or space in server name become _. Plugin servers use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*. Connector tools appear as mcp__claude_ai_<server>__<tool>. Deny rules are evaluated before allow across all scopes; a deny at any level cannot be overridden, including by --allowedTools; managed rules cannot be overridden by CLI.
facts.limits: Rules match tool name only (see parameter-scoped entry). A server named with __ or ending in _ needs the wildcard form for allow rules (bare form does not match as allow, but as deny/ask it covers both). Rule label vs canonical name: labels do not match.

facts.feature: Glob patterns in mcp__ tool names
facts.behavior: Deny and ask rules accept globs in the tool-name position matching the full name: '"mcp__*" matches every MCP tool across all servers'; a bare-name glob deny removes the tool from Claude's context. Allow rules accept globs 'only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix' with a glob-free server segment (mcp__puppeteer__*, mcp__github__get_*).
facts.limits: 'An unanchored allow glob such as "*", "B*", or "mcp__*" is skipped and doesn't auto-approve anything.' Deny glob cannot remove EndConversation while any other tool remains.

facts.behavior: Deny and ask rules can match a top-level input parameter on built-in tools with Tool(param:value) (e.g. Agent(model:opus), Bash(run_in_background:true)). 'To match a parameter on an MCP tool, pass a deny rule with --disallowedTools. When Claude Code loads a settings file, it skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses.' The skipped rule is listed in the invalid-settings dialog at interactive start and in claude doctor.
facts.limits: In settings files, ANY mcp__ rule with parentheses is dropped (docs name deny and ask context; allow rules 'continue to use each tool's own specifier syntax' and param matching is not offered for allow at all, so an mcp__ allow with parentheses is also skipped per the blanket 'skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses'). Only a CLI --disallowedTools deny can parameter-scope an MCP tool. Params must be top-level scalars; nested fields not matchable; omitted param never matches; no combined multi-param rule. Silently inert in -p runs (only warning surfaces are the interactive dialog and claude doctor).

facts.feature: Permission rules cannot see inside MCP tool arguments (settings files)
facts.behavior: Settings-file rules for MCP tools are name-level only (server or tool). Argument-level gating of an MCP call from settings needs a PreToolUse hook that reads tool_input, or a --disallowedTools CLI deny for a top-level scalar param.
facts.limits: No settings-file syntax for MCP argument content. The docs' hooks page excerpt did not show the tool_input shape for MCP tools.

facts.feature: MCP tool calls reach PreToolUse hooks
facts.behavior: 'MCP server tools appear as regular tools in tool events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied)', named mcp__<server>__<tool>. Matcher with chars outside letters/digits/_/-/space/,/| is an unanchored JS regex; 'The .* is required: a matcher like mcp__memory ... matches no tool.' Examples: mcp__memory__.*, mcp__.*__write.*. PreToolUse runs before the permission prompt for every tool except EndConversation.
facts.limits: Plugin-bundled servers are mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>; a matcher on the bare server key never fires. Hook matcher mcp__memory (no .*) matches nothing, unlike permission-rule bare-server form. Whether hooks fire under claude -p was not stated in the fetched portion (unverified). Timed-out command/http/mcp_tool PreToolUse hook does not block unless onFailure:"block".

facts.feature: PreToolUse hook decisions vs permission rules (applies to MCP tools)
facts.behavior: 'PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules': a matching deny rule blocks and a matching ask rule still prompts even if the hook returned allow or ask. A hook exit 2 'stops the tool call before permission rules are evaluated' even when an allow rule exists. Exit 0 with no output is no decision, not approval. permissionDecision values: allow/deny/ask/defer. updatedInput under hookSpecificOutput replaces the tool's arguments; PostToolUse updatedToolOutput replaces the result.
facts.limits: MCP tools marked _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction and connector tools set to ask by the org still prompt when a hook returns allow. In plan mode a hook allow does not skip prompts for non-read-only calls. Could not confirm updatedMCPToolOutput as a field name.

facts.behavior: Hook handler that calls an MCP tool (fields server, tool, optional input with ${path} substitution). Result text is read like command stdout; isError:true yields a non-blocking error. On blocking events waits for the server up to MCP_TIMEOUT and hook timeout.
facts.limits: Never starts an OAuth flow (authenticate from /mcp first). SessionStart at launch and every Setup event fire before MCP servers are available, so their mcp_tool hooks are skipped. Plugin server uses plugin:<plugin>:<server> in the server field.

facts.behavior: Elicitation hook can auto-respond to MCP server input requests (matcher is the server name); exit 2 declines with no dialog. ElicitationResult fires before the response goes back to the server. Dialogs otherwise appear automatically.
facts.limits: Not a permission control on tool calls.

facts.behavior: Server authors set _meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]: true; Claude Code shows the permission prompt on every call, even in acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions; no 'don't ask again'; allow rules and PreToolUse allow do not skip it. dontAsk denies it.
facts.limits: Server-author side, not user config. With --permission-prompt-tool an allow is converted to deny; Agent SDK canUseTool can approve.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (Require approval for a specific tool)

facts.behavior: Enabled by default: 'MCP tools are deferred and discovered on demand'; only tool names and server instructions load at start. ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: unset/true = defer all; auto = load upfront while definitions total <10% of context; auto:N custom percent; false = load all upfront. Per-server "alwaysLoad": true exempts a server (startup waits up to the 5s connect timeout); "alwaysLoad": false defers even author-marked tools (v2.1.287+). Tool author _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad. permissions.deny ["ToolSearch"] makes MCP tools load upfront. No fixed per-server tool cap.
facts.limits: Not used on models before Opus 4/Sonnet 4/Haiku 4.5 (loaded upfront; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true does not override) nor on Microsoft Foundry on Azure. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS keeps it off (managed settings can override, v2.1.227+); HIPAA config forces off. Descriptions/server instructions truncated: 4,096 chars upfront, 16,384 for tool-search-loaded tools (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH replaces both). Deferral affects context, not permissions: deferred tools still pass through permission rules and hooks (inferred from docs structure; docs do not state it explicitly).

facts.behavior: Standalone file at /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-mcp.json (macOS), /etc/claude-code/managed-mcp.json (Linux/WSL), C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-mcp.json (Windows). When present Claude Code loads only its servers, managedMcpServers, in-process app servers, and optionally Claude in Chrome. Users 'can't add, modify, or use any other MCP servers', including plugin servers and --mcp-config servers. claude mcp add fails with an enterprise-policy error. Empty mcpServers {} disables MCP.
facts.limits: Cannot be delivered via server-managed settings. Suppresses claude.ai connectors and Chrome unless allowAllClaudeAiMcps / allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp (device-level managed sources only). --mcp-config or --strict-mcp-config with the file makes Claude Code exit at startup on a workstation. Any local user can read the file; do not store secrets. allowedMcpServers does not apply to its servers (since v2.1.259) except those using ${VAR}; deniedMcpServers does. Previously configured servers vanish with no warning.

facts.behavior: Provides remote servers to every user alongside their own (v2.1.259+). Outranks local/project/user scope and same-URL plugin/connectors. Users cannot edit or remove; they can toggle off in /mcp. Needs no allowedMcpServers entry; deniedMcpServers still applies.
facts.limits: Entry must be type http/sse with https:// url, no command/args/env/headersHelper, no ${VAR}. Read only from managed sources; dropped with a warning from user/project/local files. Not read in Claude Desktop Code tab on third-party deployment or Cowork. Earlier clients ignore it.

facts.behavior: Lists of single-key entries: serverUrl (exact or * wildcards), serverCommand (exact command+args array), serverName (exact label). Evaluation: merge lists across scopes, denylist first ('Nothing overrides a denylist match'), then allowlist. Unset allowlist = all allowed; [] = none allowed. Remote servers need a serverUrl match; stdio need serverCommand; serverName counts only if no URL/command entries exist for that type. Also filters --mcp-config servers and claude.ai connectors.
facts.limits: 'A serverName entry ... is not a security control' (user picks the label). serverCommand does not compare env. Skip the allowlist: managedMcpServers, managed-mcp.json entries without ${VAR}, built-in servers (Chrome, ide), type:sdk servers skip all checks. Allowlists merge across scopes so a user can broaden unless allowManagedMcpServersOnly; denylists always merge from all scopes. Policy URL entries expand env from a pinned environment (v2.1.219+). Disappearing servers give users no signal.

facts.behavior: With allowedMcpServers in managed settings, makes the managed allowlist the only one: 'allowlists from user, project, and local settings are ignored'. Read from every admin-controlled managed source (v2.1.273+).
facts.limits: No effect outside managed sources. Separate from allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, which locks permission rules only and 'does not enforce the MCP allowlist'. Denylist still merges from all scopes.

facts.behavior: Makes managed settings the only source of permission rules (including mcp__ rules).
facts.limits: Does not restrict which MCP servers can connect. Full list of ignored sources is on settings-reference, not fetched.

facts.behavior: With true or including mcp, users cannot add servers via ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json; plugin servers and managedMcpServers still load; claude mcp add errors.
facts.limits: Details of the key are on settings-reference (not fetched).

facts.behavior: Precedence high to low: managed, command line (--settings), project local, shared project, user. List keys such as permissions.allow merge across files. disableClaudeAiConnectors: true from any scope is honored even over managed false; ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false has same effect for the shell. Servers via explicit --mcp-config unaffected by that.
facts.limits: Managed-tier source precedence is on managed-settings page (not fetched). Project-file permissions.allow waits for workspace trust; deny and ask apply right away. disableClaudeAiConnectors does not touch --mcp-config servers.

facts.feature: Workspace trust and MCP in non-interactive sessions
facts.behavior: headersHelper on a .mcp.json/local server runs only after the trust dialog; in -p/SDK it is not run and a 'headersHelper not run' line goes to stderr. Inline subagent mcpServers from repo are not used. /cd moves the session and reloads project/local MCP servers subject to same approval.
facts.limits: Servers in .mcp.json connect without asking in -p/SDK (SDK only if settingSources includes project).

facts.behavior: Warning above 10,000 tokens; default max 25,000 (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS). Over limit, saved to a file under ~/.claude/projects tool-results and replaced by a path message. Text results over 50,000 chars saved regardless; per-tool _meta anthropic/maxResultSizeChars raises up to 500,000. Error text over ~11,000 chars keeps first/last 5,000. HTTP/SSE responses over 16 MiB fail; WebSocket message over 16 MiB closes the connection.
facts.limits: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS applies only to tools without own limit; images still subject to it; does not change the 50,000-char threshold.

facts.behavior: Tools with invalid input schemas (property names not 1-64 ASCII chars, or invalid draft 2020-12) are excluded individually (v2.1.216+); root-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf schemas are flattened with a description sentence; tools whose full mcp__ name exceeds 128 chars are left out.
facts.limits: Schema exclusion depends on a feature flag fetched from Anthropic; off in air-gapped or flag-fetching-off deployments, then the API returns 400. Flattened anyOf/oneOf required lists not enforced by schema; server must validate.

facts.behavior: Servers may send list_changed; interactive terminal refetches tools/prompts/resources; -p and Agent SDK refresh only the tool list. Failed refresh keeps prior discovered items. Discovery retries up to 3 times on transient errors.
facts.limits: No retry on auth errors, 4xx, or request timeouts. Resources and prompts get only list_changed and retry coverage.

facts.behavior: Resources referenced with @server:protocol://path; Claude Code provides list/read tools when servers support them. Prompts appear as /mcp__server__prompt commands (also listed /servername:promptname (MCP)); results injected into the conversation.
facts.limits: ui:// and text/html;profile=mcp-app resources hidden from @ suggestions and list tool. Prompts from a server named anthropic-skills are hidden. Prompt arguments split on whitespace.

facts.feature: OAuth and headersHelper for remote servers
facts.behavior: 401/403 marks a server as needing auth; stored token refreshed and request retried once. claude mcp login <name> / logout; --callback-port, --client-id, --client-secret (keychain). headersHelper command must print JSON string map, 10s timeout, uncached, re-run once on 401/403, overrides static headers.
facts.limits: claude -p and SDK cannot run the OAuth flow. Rejected static Authorization header fails the connection rather than falling back to OAuth. headersHelper env strips names containing TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/KEY/AUTH for repo/plugin-supplied helpers; runs only after trust.

facts.behavior: Org setting ask: Claude Code prompts every call ('Your organization requires approval for this tool'), allow rules and hook allow do not skip it, even in auto and bypassPermissions; dontAsk denies. blocked: tool filtered out before Claude sees it.
facts.limits: Applies only in sessions where that org setting reaches Claude Code.

facts.behavior: Subcommands: add, add-json, add-from-claude-desktop (Mac/WSL), get, list, login, logout, remove, reset-project-choices, serve. add/add-json/remove take -s/--scope (local default, user, project). add takes -t/--transport (stdio default, sse, http), -e, -H, --callback-port, --client-id, --client-secret. list and get show unapproved .mcp.json servers as '⏸ Pending approval' without connecting; approved ones are health-checked.
facts.limits: remove without --scope removes from whichever scope holds it. add refuses under managed-mcp.json, denylist, or non-allowlisted server policy.

facts.behavior: Starts Claude Code as a stdio MCP server exposing Claude Code's tools to an MCP client.
facts.limits: 'Your own client is responsible for implementing user confirmation for individual tool calls.' Background command completion is not notified to the client.

facts.behavior: With OpenTelemetry export, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 includes MCP server and tool names in tool events and cost/token counters.
facts.limits: Requires configured exporter; observability only.

area: Headless and programmatic use: claude -p, output formats, --json-schema, permission modes, budget, --bare, MCP strictness, hooks/skills in print mode, agent listing, Agent SDK options (as of Claude Code 2.1.306, 2026-10-21)

facts.behavior: "Add the -p (or --print) flag to any claude command to run it non-interactively." Exits 0 on success, non-zero on failure. Invalid flags error to stderr before the run; in-run failures such as missing auth are printed as the result on stdout. --help: "The workspace trust dialog is skipped when Claude is run in non-interactive mode... Settings files that fail validation are silently ignored in this mode."
facts.limits: Not every option combines with -p: --bg is rejected, --cloud with a task description is rejected. Piped stdin capped at 10MB. SIGTERM exits 143 and records no result for the in-flight turn. Without --bare, -p discovers and loads hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP, auto memory and CLAUDE.md like an interactive session. --continue normally skips -p/SDK sessions but `claude -p --continue` includes them.

facts.behavior: text (default) plain; json = "structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata" including total_cost_usd and per-model cost; stream-json = newline-delimited events, last line is a result message. stream-json needs --verbose; --include-partial-messages, --include-hook-events, --forward-subagent-text, --replay-user-messages, --prompt-suggestions all require stream-json. system/init event lists model, tools, mcp_servers, plugins, plugin_errors, mcp_server_errors.
facts.limits: Print mode only. Cost figures are client-side estimates and may differ from the bill. --input-format stream-json is the only other input format. Skipped invalid --mcp-config entries are reported only in mcp_server_errors when stderr is redirected.

facts.behavior: "Get validated JSON output matching a JSON Schema after the agent completes its workflow (print mode only)." Result has the data in a structured_output field. Claude Code adds a StructuredOutput tool; a non-matching call returns tool_result is_error:true and the agent calls it again ("re-prompting on mismatch"). If validation does not succeed within the retry limit the result has subtype error_max_structured_output_retries (also if a model fallback retracts the output with no retry). Invalid JSON Schema: exits with "Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema" (before v2.1.205 silently ignored).
facts.limits: Validation failure does not stop the process cleanly as success: the response has no structured_output field and the subtype is an error; a result can also be subtype success with no structured_output (e.g. Claude declined), so scripts must check the field is present. The `format` keyword is accepted as an annotation and NOT enforced. SDK validates draft-07; newer $schema versions are rejected. Schema complexity limits per API JSON Schema limitations. Docs do not state the retry count or the CLI exit code on this error.

facts.behavior: "Begin in a specified permission mode." Accepts default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, or manual (alias for default, v2.1.200+). Overrides defaultMode from settings. In v2.1.302+, claude -p and SDK runs with no permission mode set start in Manual mode, where calls needing approval are denied unless approved by an allow rule, hook, canUseTool callback, or --permission-prompt-tool.
facts.limits: dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt, but reads in working dirs, the read-only command set, and --allowedTools/permissions.allow matches still run; AskUserQuestion, org-'ask' connector tools, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools and network-path reads are denied even with an allow rule; an installed mod can still approve some calls. acceptEdits does not auto-approve other shell commands or network requests. In -p, auto mode has no prompt fallback: when repeated classifier blocks reach a threshold the action does not run and Claude keeps working (run is not stopped); auto-mode deletion-type prompts are denied immediately. Plan mode keeps its blocks in -p. Protected-path writes are never auto-approved except in bypassPermissions. Deny rules block in every mode including bypassPermissions.

facts.behavior: "Skip permission prompts. Equivalent to --permission-mode bypassPermissions." Docs show `claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions` for unattended runs, requiring a container/VM/sandbox runtime and a non-root user on Linux/macOS. In a -p run the few calls that would still prompt are denied instead.
facts.limits: Not a bypass of everything: deny rules, protected-path and cross-session-messaging safeguards, and the other 'actions no mode auto-approves' still apply. Cloud sessions ignore this mode from settings files.

facts.behavior: --allowedTools: tools that "execute without prompting"; Read/Edit/Bash listed means no prompt (except network-path reads); uses permission rule syntax, `Bash(git diff *)` prefix match (space before * matters). In auto mode a bare Bash allow entry is dropped as a broad allow rule. --disallowedTools: bare name removes the tool from Claude's context ("*" removes all, "mcp__*" removes every MCP tool); scoped rule like Bash(rm *) leaves the tool and denies matching calls. --tools restricts the built-in set ("" disables all).
facts.limits: --tools does not affect MCP tools (use --disallowedTools "mcp__*"). Bash argument-constraining patterns are "fragile". MCP permission rules match at server or tool-name level only (mcp__server, mcp__server__*, mcp__server__tool); to match a parameter of an MCP tool the docs say use --disallowedTools, and a settings-file mcp__ rule containing parentheses is skipped (listed as invalid, only surfaced in the interactive invalid-settings dialog and claude doctor). Allow globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix; unanchored allow globs like mcp__* are skipped. Built-in tools support Tool(param:value) deny/ask rules; MCP tools do not.

facts.behavior: --permission-prompt-tool: "Specify an MCP tool to handle permission prompts in non-interactive mode" (mcp__<server>__<tool>). --permission-prompts host|none (v2.1.259+): none means "anything that would prompt is denied automatically; the permission mode still decides everything else"; Claude is told nobody can approve and not to retry; AskUserQuestion is removed; unanswered MCP elicitation is cancelled; denials appear as permission_denied messages / permission_denials in result.
facts.limits: Rules, PermissionRequest hooks and the mode still decide first; a PermissionRequest hook can still allow under none. Prompt tool cannot approve requiresUserInteraction MCP tools (allow converted to deny, v2.1.199+). Print mode only.

facts.behavior: "Stop the run once estimated spend on API calls reaches this amount (print mode only)." Subagent spend counts. Once reached, spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached` and background subagents are stopped (v2.1.217+); the run stops waiting on background work.
facts.limits: Checked against a client-side cost estimate, "can differ from your bill"; "Spend can pass the cap, so leave headroom". On --continue/--resume, totals restored from earlier runs do not count toward the cap. Print mode only; no interactive equivalent. --max-turns is a separate print-only cap that "Exits with an error when the limit is reached".

facts.behavior: "Skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md." --help adds LSP, plugin sync, attribution, keychain reads, background prefetches; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1. Claude has Bash, file read and file edit tools. Only command-line MCP servers connect; no system reminders (no skill list, no file-changed notices); no background tasks. Context is supplied via --append-system-prompt[-file], --settings, --mcp-config, --agents, --plugin-dir/--plugin-url, --add-dir. Docs: "the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release."
facts.limits: Skills still resolve via /skill-name; skills in an --add-dir .claude/skills/ still load, but its commands/ and agents/ do not. Auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (no OAuth/keychain); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry use own creds. The project's env block and helpers like awsAuthRefresh still apply. 'Features built into Claude Code are unaffected' (built-in hooks/behaviors). Before v2.1.286 the MCP/reminder/background limits held only partly. System prompt snapshot recording is off under --bare unless --system-prompt-snapshot on. Differs from --safe-mode, which keeps auth/model/permissions and disables customizations including managed-plugin/skill paths.

facts.behavior: --strict-mcp-config: "Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config, ignoring all other MCP configurations." --mcp-config loads servers from JSON files/strings; with -p Claude Code waits for pending servers before the first turn up to MCP_TIMEOUT (default 30s, v2.1.221+); invalid entries are skipped and reported in mcp_server_errors, run still exits cleanly.
facts.limits: Without --bare or --strict-mcp-config, -p connects servers in the project's .mcp.json even in an untrusted folder, with no per-server approval prompt. claude.ai connectors still load unless strictMcpConfig, disableClaudeAiConnectors or ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false (SDK doc says mcpServers: {} does not suppress them). Behavior under a managed-mcp.json is on a separate page (managed-mcp). --restricted help says add --strict-mcp-config to skip MCP servers.

facts.behavior: Without --bare, -p runs hooks from project .claude/settings.json (and user settings) "even in a folder you've never trusted"; SessionStart and Setup hooks stream as hook_started/progress/response events always; --include-hook-events adds others (stream-json only). SessionStart hook initialUserMessage can supply the first turn in -p. SIGTERM runs only SessionEnd hooks. Setup hooks fire with --init/--maintenance (print only) or --init-only. Hook types: command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent. Exit 2 blocks on blockable events (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, etc.).
facts.limits: Docs do not state which other events fire under -p (Stop, PermissionRequest, Elicitation) beyond the above; page read was truncated. Exit code 1 is non-blocking; failing/timed-out hooks do not block unless onFailure:"block" (v2.1.295+). Exit 2 not honored for PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, SessionStart, Setup, Notification, SessionEnd etc. Frontmatter hooks in project subagents/@skills-dir plugins are not used in an untrusted -p folder, but a project skill's hooks are used. terminalSequence ignored in -p. To disable: --bare, or --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' (user-settings alone is not enough since project settings override), or --setting-sources user. Agent SDK callback hooks that time out block the tool call.

facts.feature: Skills, slash commands and output styles in print mode
facts.behavior: "User-invoked skills and custom commands work. Include /skill-name in the prompt string and Claude Code expands it before running." Built-in terminal-UI commands like /login are unavailable. /model, /effort, /fast, /color, /rename take an argument; /mcp with no argument prints a text summary; /config key=value changes a setting; /output-style <style> switches output style (v2.1.269+). Without --bare, skills are discovered as in interactive sessions. --disable-slash-commands disables all skills and commands. Forked skills started via /skill-name emit messages with parent_tool_use_id starting 'forked-command-' (v2.1.287+).
facts.limits: With --bare Claude gets no skill list (system reminder omitted), so only explicit /skill-name works. Docs on this page do not say whether an output style rewrites or appends to the system prompt (see output-styles page, not read). --safe-mode disables skills, output styles, commands.

facts.feature: System prompt flags in print mode
facts.behavior: --system-prompt / --system-prompt-file replace the entire default prompt; --append-system-prompt / --append-system-prompt-file append (default tool guidance, safety instructions and coding conventions preserved). Can combine replace + append; v2.1.283+ allows flag plus its own file form. --append-subagent-system-prompt[-file] appends to every subagent prompt, -p only. --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections moves cwd/env/memory paths/git status into the first user message for cache reuse, default prompt only.
facts.limits: Replacing drops tool guidance and safety instructions, and the git status snapshot. The prompt is recorded on the conversation's first request and reused on --resume/--continue until compaction, so changed flag text on resume has no effect unless --system-prompt-snapshot off. Recording is off under --bare.

facts.feature: Workspace trust and untrusted-folder behavior in -p
facts.behavior: A claude -p or SDK run never shows the trust dialog. Used without trust: settings-file hooks, env block, apiKeyHelper, project skill hooks and allowed-tools, .mcp.json servers (connected without asking). Not used: permissions.allow rules and additionalDirectories in project settings (stderr warning 'this workspace has not been trusted'), frontmatter hooks of project subagents, inline subagent mcpServers, headersHelper.
facts.limits: Mitigations are advisory-by-flag: --setting-sources user, --bare, --settings disableAllHooks, disabledMcpjsonServers. --restricted (v2.1.248+) removes command-running tools and WebFetch, confines file tools to working dirs, loads only managed settings and --settings, refuses bypassPermissions.

facts.feature: Session persistence and resume in print mode
facts.behavior: --no-session-persistence: sessions "are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed" (print mode only). --continue/--resume work with -p; session_id is in json output. --resume accepts ID, name, or transcript .jsonl path. Background work (commands, subagents, Monitor, /loop wakeups) can keep the run open after the turn; 10-minute idle cap by default (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS).
facts.limits: Total cost on resume reports the whole conversation. CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY does the same in any mode.

facts.feature: How a print-mode run is labeled in the agent listing (claude agents / agent view)
facts.behavior: Agent view documents only two kind values: interactive and background (claude agents --json fields: cwd, kind, startedAt always; id/state for background). `--bg` combined with -p/--print is rejected "because --print never starts the interactive session that claude agents attaches to." /status Session kind reads 'background job · attached/unattended' or 'interactive'.
facts.limits: The docs say nothing about a print/SDK label, an entrypoint field, or whether -p runs appear in the listing at all; a -p run is not a background session. Treat any claim about how -p runs are labeled as undocumented. Only the first ~100k characters of the agent-view page were read.

facts.feature: Agent SDK: settingSources and what loads by default
facts.behavior: "When you omit settingSources, query() reads the same filesystem settings as the Claude Code CLI: user, project, and local settings, CLAUDE.md files, and .claude/ skills, agents, and commands." Omitting equals ["user","project","local"]. settingSources: [] limits the agent to what is configured programmatically. Project settings.json and hooks load only from <cwd>/.claude/ (no parent fallback); CLAUDE.md/rules load from cwd and parents. Skills: when the `skills` option is omitted, discovered user and project skills are enabled and the Skill tool is available; skills option accepts "all", a list, or [].
facts.limits: Read regardless of settingSources: managed policy settings (MDM/registry/file and server-managed), ~/.claude.json, auto memory (disable with autoMemoryEnabled:false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1), claude.ai MCP connectors (disable with strictMcpConfig: true), sandbox credential deny/mask entries. Docs warn not to rely on defaults for multi-tenant isolation. Skills cannot be registered programmatically; filesystem only. TypeScript SDK supports more hook events than Python (SessionStart, SessionEnd, TeammateIdle, TaskCompleted).

facts.feature: Agent SDK: options (permissionMode, allowedTools, hooks, outputFormat, mcpServers, agents)
facts.behavior: Same engine as claude -p (SDK "runs the Claude Code binary"). Options referenced in docs: permissionMode/permission_mode (default = Manual; 'auto' supported), allowedTools/allowed_tools (allow rules), canUseTool callback (permission host), outputFormat/output_format {type:'json_schema', schema}, hooks (programmatic callbacks, run alongside filesystem hooks, also fire inside subagents with agent_id/agent_type), mcpServers, strictMcpConfig, agents + allowedTools ['Agent'] for subagents, settingSources, skills, tools, additionalDirectories (passed as --add-dir), cwd, env, systemPrompt. Programmatic hook returns permissionDecision 'deny' with reason to block a tool.
facts.limits: The docs URL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sdk returned 404 (moved to /docs/en/agent-sdk/overview and /docs/en/headless). Full per-option reference lives in /agent-sdk/typescript and /agent-sdk/python, which were not fetched, so maxBudgetUsd/maxTurns option names are not confirmed here. Agent teams are not configurable via SDK options. Unless approved, third parties may not offer claude.ai login in SDK products (API key auth). SDK hooks 'fire in the main agent and any subagents'.

facts.behavior: --max-turns: limit agentic turns, print only, exits with an error when reached, no limit by default. --fallback-model: automatic fallback list when primary overloaded/unavailable. --agents accepts JSON or (with --print, v2.1.281+) a file path; validated at startup (v2.1.242+). --settings: file or inline JSON overriding same keys in settings files. --setting-sources user,project,local selects sources. --model / --effort override settings for the session without persisting.
facts.limits: --max-turns is print-only. --settings file must be a regular file under 2 MiB. Managed settings outrank command-line arguments for permission rules ("no other level, including command line arguments, can override a managed permission rule").

area: Workflow tool, bundled workflows and review skills (/deep-research, /code-review local and ultra, /security-review, /simplify, /verify), resumeFromRunId, workflow agent model resolution, CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL

facts.behavior: "A dynamic workflow is a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents at once. Claude writes the script for the task you describe, and a runtime executes it in the background while your session stays responsive." Intermediate results stay in script variables, not Claude's context. Every run writes its script under the session's directory in ~/.claude/projects/.
facts.limits: Script runs isolated: no mid-run user input, no direct filesystem or shell access from the script itself (agents do that), no module loading (import() fails before run). Date.now(), Math.random(), no-arg new Date() throw so relaunch repeats the same agent() calls. Available on paid plans, API, Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry; Pro must turn on in /config.

facts.behavior: "Claude can start a workflow only from a script file the session is already allowed to read. To run a script kept outside your working directory, add its directory with /add-dir or a Read allow rule first." (The house deep-research-pinned skill states the Workflow tool runs a script inside the working directory, an added directory, or the scratchpad; the docs page itself only states the readable-file rule.)
facts.limits: No other path is documented as allowed.

facts.behavior: Per-run prompt shows planned phases: Yes run it / Yes and don't ask again for <name> in <path> (only for bundled, saved, or plugin workflows by name) / View raw script / No. Auto mode: first launch only, consent recorded in user settings, skipped when ultracode on. Manual and accept-edits: every run. Bypass permissions: no prompt. In claude -p and Agent SDK there is no prompt: Workflow call goes through normal permission evaluation (deny/ask rules, dontAsk apply); to allow add `Workflow` or `Workflow(<name>)` allow rule, auto mode, bypass mode, a PreToolUse hook returning allow (not enough alone in plan mode), --permission-prompt-tool or canUseTool. Subagents the workflow spawns use the user's permission rules; "the agents' tool calls receive the same permission checks and sandboxing as any other tool call in the session."
facts.limits: The ultracode keyword does not change permissions. In auto mode the script-computed agent() prompt does not count as a user request for the classifier.

facts.behavior: The Workflow tool is removed from every subagent, even when listed in the tools field (sub-agents page, available-tools first filter).
facts.limits: Only the main session (or script) launches workflows.

facts.behavior: Keyword `ultracode` in a typed prompt (or asking 'use a workflow') makes Claude write a workflow for that task. `/effort ultracode` plans a workflow for every substantive task in the session. While on: Large workflow warning not shown, concurrent subagent limit not enforced for Agent-tool spawns, auto mode does not ask to approve first workflow launch.
facts.limits: Keyword is opt-in only in human-typed input (interactive prompt, IDE panel, Remote Control, SDK with origin human). It does NOT trigger from -p prompts, unstamped SDK prompts, scheduled task prompts, or webhook/PR-comment payloads. Raises token use.

facts.behavior: Up to 16 concurrent agents by default (fewer on fewer CPUs); CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS 1 to 256 (v2.1.269+). Up to 4,096 items in one parallel()/pipeline() call (longer list rejected with an error). 1,000 agents total per run. Schema retries: MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES default 5. Stalled agent restarts automatically up to 5 times (stallMs per agent or CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS).
facts.limits: Caps are hard runtime limits. Docs: workflow agents follow their own limits, not CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS.

facts.feature: Large workflow warning and size guideline
facts.behavior: Progress line shows `Large workflow` when more than 25 agents are scheduled or projected tokens pass 1.5 million. "The warning is advisory: it doesn't pause or limit the run." workflowSizeGuideline (unrestricted, small <5, medium <10, large <50) is advice to Claude when writing the script; default medium, small on Pro (v2.1.271+).
facts.limits: Guideline is "advice, not a cap"; runtime caps apply regardless.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code picks each workflow agent's model in the same order it uses for subagents. A model the script names for a stage counts as the per-invocation model in that order. When nothing else assigns one, the agent runs on your session's model." Subagent order (v2.1.251+): 1 per-invocation model parameter, 2 agent definition model frontmatter (inherit = main model), 3 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (alias or ID), 4 main conversation's model. availableModels allowlist substitution applies to workflow agents (blocked family alias -> newest permitted version of family; other blocked value -> inherited model; interactive warning shown).
facts.limits: Before v2.1.251 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL came first and overrode per-invocation and frontmatter. A family alias (e.g. opus) in per-invocation/frontmatter resolves to the main conversation's exact model when the main model is in that family. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL alone does not change built-in Explore and Plan.

facts.behavior: "The default model for subagents, agent team teammates, and workflow agents that aren't assigned a model another way. Accepts an alias such as haiku or a full model name. Two sources take precedence over it: a model Claude passes when it spawns the agent, and a model field in the agent's definition, including inherit." `inherit` equals unset.
facts.limits: A default, not an override (since v2.1.251). An alias here always resolves to the alias's pointed version even if it names the main model's family.

facts.behavior: Set to 1 (v2.1.257+) to force one model onto subagents, teammates, and workflow agents. With both vars set, models run on CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL; with only FORCE, they run on the main conversation's model (built-in Explore keeps its listed model). While on, "Claude Code ignores the model field in subagent definitions, and Claude can't pass a model when it starts a subagent."
facts.limits: Forks and skills running in a subagent with model: inherit still use the main model.

facts.behavior: NOT DOCUMENTED on the env-vars, workflows, sub-agents or skills pages fetched 2026-10-21 (the env-vars page was read in full via two fetches; the only WORKFLOW env vars listed are CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS, CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS, CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS). No docs behavior can be cited. Prior local research notes in this repo (not docs) say the 2.1.296 binary, when this is set to anything but inherit, drops both per-call model and agent-definition model for workflow agents and logs that the named model was ignored.
facts.limits: Treat as undocumented; binary-derived behavior is unverified by docs.

facts.behavior: Docs describe resume behavior but do not use the name `resumeFromRunId` on the workflows page. Replay is in agent start order: completed agent returns saved result; the first agent whose prompt differs (script edited or earlier agent returned something different) reruns and so does every agent after it; still-running at stop starts over; failed agent reruns and so does every agent started after it (stopping one agent with x counts as failing). Pause/resume with `p` in /workflows; stopped run is resumed by asking Claude to relaunch with the same script; relaunch refused until the stopped agents exit. Resumable within the same session; with `claude --resume` saved results under ~/.claude/projects/ can replay; in a fresh session Claude starts a new run. Cloud sessions keep results with conversation history.
facts.limits: If saved results can't be found the relaunch fails with `nothing to resume` rather than starting over. Before v2.1.305 completed agents could rerun on an unedited script whose pipeline()/parallel() items ran more than one agent each. A reordered script reruns from the first divergence.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#resume-after-a-pause ; Agent SDK reference #workflow (not fetched) for tool inputs

facts.behavior: On a claude.ai usage limit, agents wait for the reset and the run continues (v2.1.271+).
facts.limits: Only interactive claude.ai-subscription sessions with autoContinueAtUsageLimit on, reset within 24 h, and not already waited twice. Not in -p, Agent SDK, background sessions, Remote Control or agent-team teammates: the agent fails.

facts.behavior: /workflows then `s` saves a run's script to .claude/workflows/ (project) or ~/.claude/workflows/ (personal); runs as /<name>. Project beats personal on same name; closest .claude/workflows/ to cwd wins in monorepos. Plugin workflows live in workflows/ at plugin root and are namespaced /<plugin>:<meta.name>. `meta` must be a plain literal object first statement or /<name> is dropped from autocomplete. /reload-skills re-reads workflow dirs.
facts.limits: Symlinked save targets refused. Saved workflows take input via the `args` global.

facts.behavior: disableWorkflows: true (user or managed settings), /config toggle, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1. Then /workflows, workflow commands and /workflow-authoring are unavailable, ultracode keyword and toggle removed.
facts.limits: A run already in progress keeps going. No managed setting disables ultracode alone.

facts.behavior: Loads the reference for writing workflow scripts (script API, resume, quality patterns, examples). Claude normally loads it itself before writing a script; run it before hand-editing a saved script. Requires v2.1.248+ and workflows enabled.
facts.limits: Reference only; per the skill listing it does not itself authorize running a workflow.

facts.behavior: "Fans out web searches on a question across several angles, fetches and cross-checks the sources it finds, votes on each claim, and returns a cited report with claims that didn't survive cross-checking filtered out." Claims verifiers cannot check (rate limit, API error) are listed as unverified, not refuted.
facts.limits: "Requires the WebSearch tool to be available." "runs only when you invoke it." Docs name no depth/model/budget args; those belong to the house fork. Name collision: a user/project skill or workflow with the same name replaces the bundled command (not aliases).

facts.behavior: Reviews branch changes (commits ahead of upstream plus uncommitted; falls back to main or previous commit) for correctness bugs; depending on model and effort also reuse, simplification, efficiency cleanups. Runs as a background forked subagent with own context; findings arrive as text (or via ReportFindings tool when a host requests it, v2.1.218+). Targets: PR number, branch, path, revision range. Levels low|medium|high|xhigh|max; low reports only most confident findings. With no level typed it reuses the last typed level (even from earlier session); ultra neither uses nor updates it; -p runs don't update it. Flags: --fix (apply findings, via permission mode), --comment (inline GitHub PR comments or one GitLab MR note via glab, v2.1.257+), --max-findings n|all|default (v2.1.288+; limit 32 via findings tool; remembered except in -p). /review is an alias.
facts.limits: Without --fix, instructions ask for report only (advisory instruction, edits go through permission mode). Background --fix edits are outside /rewind checkpoints. Follows CLAUDE.md (including -p) but does NOT read REVIEW.md (that is for the managed GitHub Code Review service). Runs foreground in -p, with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, or when rerun during an active review. Claude may start it on its own or from a session-scoped scheduled task (never the cloud review); stop with skillOverrides {"code-review":"user-invocable-only"}. Bundled body is not on disk/editable. A project/personal skill named code-review replaces it but the /review alias still runs the bundled review.

facts.behavior: `/code-review ultra [--fix] [--post] [base-branch|PR#|note]` runs deeper multi-agent review in the cloud comparing current branch against the repo default branch plus uncommitted and staged changes; --post (v2.1.227+) preselects posting findings to a github.com PR from the user's GitHub account. Single word after ultra = base branch or PR number; longer text becomes a note. `claude ultrareview` subcommand waits and prints findings for scripts/CI.
facts.limits: Needs claude.ai auth. Not on Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry, ZDR orgs, HIPAA config, or CMEK orgs; where unavailable, `/code-review ultra` runs a local review instead (CMEK: cannot run). Non-interactive -p does not wait for the cloud review. Uncommitted credential-like files (.env, *.tfvars) follow the cloud-session upload rules. Scheduled tasks never launch it.

facts.behavior: "Analyze the changes on your current branch for security vulnerabilities. Reviews the diff between your branch and origin's default branch, identifying risks like injection, auth issues, and data exposure." Also available through the Skill tool (listed among built-in commands reachable that way). It injects dynamic shell context (errors 'Shell command failed for pattern' map to it).
facts.limits: Needs an `origin` remote; fails with an `ambiguous argument` error when origin HEAD is unset. Listed in commands reference as a command, not marked Skill. The dedicated URL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security-review returned 404; no moved page found via search of fetched pages. Review is advice/report, not enforcement.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors (security-review-fails-without-origin-head, section body not read)

facts.behavior: "Review the changed code for cleanup opportunities and apply the fixes. Four review agents run in parallel, covering reuse of existing helpers, simplification, efficiency, and whether the change is at the right level of abstraction." Optional path or PR reference target.
facts.limits: "The review doesn't look for correctness bugs. Use /code-review." Was named /simplify before v2.1.147 when it applied fixes by default for bug-finding; scripts should use /code-review --fix. The bundled /simplify does not trigger the pre-commit run; a user/project/personal skill or .claude/commands file named simplify does.

facts.feature: /verify (bundled skill) and where it writes its recipe
facts.behavior: "Build and run your app to confirm a code change does what it should, without falling back to tests or type checks." Works without setup by inferring launch from project type, README, package.json, Makefile. "When it has to build and drive your app without a recorded recipe, it writes what worked to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md at the repo root, or in the touched package directory in a monorepo." Claude edits the file only when it steered a run wrong, so it can be committed. /run-skill-generator separately records a per-project recipe at .claude/skills/run-<name>/ that /run, /verify and other agents follow. Runs only when invoked by the user.
facts.limits: "At the repo root, the recorded skill replaces the bundled /verify" (a repo skill named verify replaces it); a recording in a monorepo package directory does not replace the bundled one. Inference is unreliable for apps needing a database, env file, graphical session, or multi-step build.

facts.behavior: "When a session starts with a skill named verify or simplify in place, Claude Code's commit instructions tell Claude to run it right before each commit, except for changes to docs or tests." Requires v2.1.286+.
facts.limits: Counts only skills from enterprise, personal, project or additional-directory locations or .claude/commands files; the repo-root recorded verify recipe counts. Bundled /verify and /simplify, plugin skills, and claude.ai account skills do not count. Skill must be model-invocable (disable-model-invocation: true removes it). includeGitInstructions off removes it. It is an instruction to Claude, not a hook.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (Run your checks before each commit)

facts.feature: Bundled skill override and disable rules
facts.behavior: Same-name skill replaces the bundled command but not its aliases; enterprise > personal > project; plugin skills namespaced so both load. disableBundledSkills setting turns bundled skills off. Deny rule Skill(review) also blocks bundled /code-review via its /review alias. skillOverrides entries under an alias honored only in managed settings or a --settings file.
facts.limits: Some bundled skills (e.g. /verify) run only when the user invokes them; others Claude may invoke automatically.

facts.behavior: Researches, decomposes work into 5 to 30 independent units, presents a plan, and after approval spawns one background subagent per unit in an isolated worktree; each implements, runs tests and publishes its change.
facts.limits: Requires a git repository or a WorktreeCreate hook (outside git needs v2.1.281+).
