area: Scheduled and remote work: routines (/schedule), /loop, Monitor, Claude Code on the web, Remote Control, GitHub Actions, cloud session reach (as of 2026-10-21)

facts.behavior: A saved configuration (prompt, repos, connectors) that runs as a full Claude Code cloud session on Anthropic-managed infrastructure (or a self-hosted environment). Triggers: schedule, API (HTTP POST), GitHub events; one task can combine them. 'Scheduled tasks run autonomously as full Claude Code cloud sessions. You don't choose a permission mode.' Shell commands, skills and included connectors run 'without stopping for approval apart from some artifact actions'. Research preview.
facts.limits: Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only. Belongs to one claude.ai account, not shared with teammates; actions appear as you. Not available with Console API key, cloud-provider logins, or inside a cloud session. Team/Enterprise Owners can disable org-wide (server-side, cannot be overridden locally). ZDR/HIPAA/CMEK orgs cannot use cloud sessions. Reach is bounded by selected repos, the environment's network/variables, and included connectors.

facts.feature: Routine saved prompt is not live user input
facts.behavior: 'The fired prompt is therefore not live user input and can't act as approval or consent for actions during the run.' Trigger attests only that an authorized session stored the prompt ahead of time. Content fetched during the run keeps normal handling.
facts.limits: The prompt must be self-contained; no human is present to approve.

facts.behavior: Recurring cadence or one-off timestamp; times entered in local zone and converted. 'The minimum interval is one hour; expressions that run more frequently are rejected.' Custom cron via /schedule update. Exactly-on-the-hour runs 'can start several minutes late'; one-off runs turn themselves off and show Completed. If GitHub connection is missing/expired, runs are skipped for up to 72 hours, then the task turns off.
facts.limits: No sub-hourly schedules. No guarantee of exact start time.

facts.behavior: Per-task bearer token; POST to /v1/claude_code/routines/<id>/fire with beta header experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 starts a session and returns session URL. Optional freeform 'text' is wrapped in a <routine-fire-payload> block labeled untrusted data; the saved prompt must explicitly reference it to act on it.
facts.limits: Add/manage API trigger and token on the web only, not CLI. Token shown once. Claude.ai users only, not Claude Platform API. Experimental header; shapes and limits may change.

facts.behavior: Starts a new independent session per matching event. Events: pull_request (opened, closed, assigned, labeled, synchronized, etc.) and release. Filters (all must match): author, title, body, base branch, head branch, labels, is draft, is merged; operators include equals, contains, starts with, is one of, matches regex (regex tests the entire field).
facts.limits: Only pull request and release events. Requires Claude GitHub App installed on the repo (/web-setup does not install it). 'GitHub webhook events are subject to per-task and per-account hourly caps. Events beyond the limit are dropped.' CLI attach requires v2.1.225+.

facts.behavior: Scheduled runs incl. one-off: 100/hour per account (run waits). Run now + API fires + re-running a one-off: 30/hour per task (shared count), 100/hour per account for Run now, API fires 100/hour per account counted separately. 'None of these hourly limits has overage.' Runs also draw subscription usage; with usage credits on, can continue on metered overage, otherwise additional runs rejected until window resets.
facts.limits: Paused subscription puts tasks on hold.

facts.behavior: Each selected repo is cloned every run from default branch (PR head commit for PR-triggered first repo). Claude pushes to 'claude/'-prefixed branches unless the prompt directs otherwise. 'To control which branches a run can push to, use branch protection rules or rulesets on GitHub'; GitHub applies them to the connected access, so a rule that access can bypass does not block the push.
facts.limits: The claude/ prefix is default behavior of the prompt/session, not a hard push restriction; enforcement of branch limits is GitHub-side. Green run status means only that the session exited without infrastructure error, not that the work succeeded.

facts.behavior: All connected claude.ai connectors are included by default; 'Claude can use every tool from an included connector, including writes, without asking for permission during a run.' Connector traffic goes through Anthropic servers so needs no network allowlist changes.
facts.limits: Local `claude mcp add` servers are not connectors; use claude.ai connectors or a committed .mcp.json (single repo outside a project only; a task in a project does not load .mcp.json).

facts.behavior: Scheduled/Run now runs may publish a new artifact without asking (private to you); republishing an existing one without asking only when a list of conditions holds. Runs from API or GitHub triggers always ask first. Publishes declaring runtime capabilities ask first.
facts.limits: Narrow exception to the no-approval rule.

facts.behavior: Re-runs a prompt on an interval within an open session. Fixed interval (s/m/h/d; seconds rounded up to a minute; converted to cron), or prompt-only with Claude choosing a delay of 1 minute to 1 hour each iteration, or bare /loop running a built-in maintenance prompt or .claude/loop.md (project) / ~/.claude/loop.md (user), truncated beyond 25,000 bytes. Fires 'between your turns, not while Claude is mid-response', at low priority.
facts.limits: Only fires while Claude Code is running and idle; closing the terminal stops it (backgrounding the session carries it over). No catch-up: a missed run fires once when idle. Only skills Claude may invoke itself run; built-in commands (/model, /clear), disable-model-invocation skills, skillOverrides/Skill-deny skills and MCP prompts reach Claude as plain text. Min interval 1 minute. Self-paced /loop not restored on --resume; background Bash and monitor tasks never restored. Inherits session permission prompts.

facts.behavior: Underlying tools: 5-field cron, recurring or one-shot, 8-character task IDs. Local timezone. Resume with --resume/--continue restores unexpired tasks.
facts.limits: Up to 50 scheduled tasks per session. No L, W, ?, or name aliases. Day-of-month and day-of-week use OR semantics when both constrained. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 disables the scheduler, cron tools and /loop and stops already-scheduled tasks.

facts.behavior: Recurring tasks run late by up to half the gap to next run, max 30 minutes (except */5 which runs 4m45s after previous). One-shot tasks on :00/:30 run up to 90 seconds early. 'Recurring tasks automatically expire 7 days after creation. The task fires one final time, then deletes itself.'
facts.limits: For durable scheduling use cloud or Desktop scheduled tasks. Schedule off the hour for timing precision.

facts.behavior: Cloud: Anthropic cloud, machine off OK, fresh clone only (no local files), connectors per task, no permission prompts, min 1 hour. Desktop: your machine, local files, configurable permission prompts, min 1 minute. /loop: your machine, needs open session, inherits session MCP and permissions, min 1 minute.
facts.limits: Cloud tasks cannot see uncommitted local files or ~/.claude config.

facts.behavior: Runs a command in the background (or opens a WebSocket via a 'ws' input) and feeds each output line back to Claude mid-conversation. Uses the same permission rules as Bash: Bash allow/deny patterns apply to Monitor commands. Every watch has a deadline: 5 minutes default, max 30 minutes, max 10 minutes in non-interactive -p runs; at the deadline one notice is sent. Plugins can declare auto-start monitors. Dynamic /loop may use it to avoid polling.
facts.limits: Not available on Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, or Foundry, nor when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC is set; on Windows needs Git Bash. In auto mode, allow rules naming Monitor itself are set aside and the classifier reviews commands like Bash. WebSocket: ws/wss only, prompts for approval (no 'skip for this host' option), text messages become events, binary replaced by placeholder, messages over 1 MiB end the watch, private/link-local/metadata addresses and sandbox deniedDomains hosts denied. Counts against CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT on Linux/WSL (v2.1.233+; capped from v2.1.246). Stopped with the session or via TaskStop; monitors not restored on resume.

facts.feature: Claude Code on the web / cloud sessions
facts.behavior: Session runs in an isolated Anthropic-managed Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 VM (or self-hosted environment) and keeps running after laptop closes. Started from browser, mobile, Desktop, `claude --cloud`, or scheduled tasks. Fresh clone of the repo each session. Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise (premium/Chat+Claude Code seats). Shares plan rate limits; no separate VM charge. Permission mode chosen per session via dropdown.
facts.limits: GitHub required for clone and PR creation (GHES on Team/Enterprise); non-GitHub repos only as a local bundle (CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1) and cannot push back. --cloud needs claude.ai login; unavailable on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry. Not for ZDR/HIPAA/CMEK orgs. Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions fail with org IP allowlisting on. Resources approx 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Sessions stop after inactivity (including while waiting for an MCP tool approval); reopening gives a fresh VM with history restored but background work, subagents, shell commands and self-paced /loop wakeups not restored.

facts.feature: What carries into a cloud session (config reach)
facts.behavior: Available: repo CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, .claude/skills|agents|commands, repo .claude/settings.json hooks and permission rules and repo .mcp.json (single-repo sessions), org server-managed settings (not in Claude Tag sessions). Setup script can write ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md in the VM. Skills enabled on claude.ai load automatically.
facts.limits: NOT available: user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/skills|agents|commands, user-level settings and user-scoped hooks, user-scoped enabledPlugins, MCP servers from `claude mcp add` at local/user scope, plugins/marketplaces declared in repo settings.json (cloud session does not install them), MDM/managed files on your device. Multi-repo sessions do not load any repo's .claude/settings.json hooks; project threads load only root CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md and non-path-specific rules, and no repo settings hooks or .mcp.json. Commands that are terminal-only (/plugin, /resume) and /clear are unavailable; /compact and /context work; /config opens web settings. CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE is set by the cloud and overrides user value.

facts.behavior: Repo and server-managed hooks run in Anthropic-hosted sessions; SessionStart hooks 'behave the same in the cloud as locally' with caveats. Hooks run in both local and cloud; CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true lets a hook detect cloud and exit early otherwise. Setup scripts run before hooks.
facts.limits: User-level ~/.claude/settings.json hooks do not run. SessionStart command hooks cancelled after 600 s unless timeout set (not enforced for async:true). Hooks need network access for installs (None level breaks them). Multi-repo and project-thread sessions skip repo-defined hooks. Self-hosted environments additionally run operator-seeded hooks from the runner host.

facts.behavior: Four levels: None (no outbound through session network), Trusted (default allowlist of package registries, GitHub, cloud SDKs), Full, Custom allowlist. Default environment is Trusted. Blocked hosts fail with 403 and x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed.
facts.limits: Regardless of level, sessions can still reach GitHub via a separate proxy, enabled MCP connectors (via Anthropic servers), hosts listed in network secrets, and the Anthropic API even at None. Environment variables are visible to anyone using the environment; secrets belong in network secrets (Anthropic-hosted only; not self-hosted). Git credentials never enter the VM.

facts.behavior: No environment command timeout of its own; Bash defaults apply: 2 minutes default foreground, up to 10 minutes; a timed-out command moves to background (unless it starts with sleep) and can run up to 30 more minutes. Raise via BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS env vars. Setup script is cached only if it finishes in roughly 5 minutes; cache is a filesystem snapshot (background processes lost).
facts.limits: Applies to Anthropic-hosted environments.

facts.behavior: `claude --cloud "task"` creates a cloud session cloning the current directory's GitHub remote at the current branch (not local checkout; unpushed commits missing). `claude -p "msg" --cloud <id>` queues a message to an existing session and exits. `--teleport`, /teleport, /tasks t pull a cloud session into the terminal with its branch and history; the terminal copy is separate and new work there does not appear in the cloud session.
facts.limits: Handoff is one-way from CLI (cannot push a terminal session to cloud; Desktop can). Teleport needs clean git state, same repo (not fork), branch pushed, same claude.ai account. Bundle upload under 100 MB, excludes untracked files and, on macOS/Linux/WSL, uncommitted .env/key files.

facts.behavior: Claude subscribes to GitHub activity on a PR and responds to CI failures and review comments: pushes a fix if clear, asks if ambiguous, notes duplicates. Enabled per PR (CI status bar, /autofix-pr, mobile, or pasted PR URL). Replies to review threads post under your GitHub account labeled as Claude Code.
facts.limits: Requires Claude GitHub App on the repo. No webhook for base-branch merge conflicts, so it cannot react to them. Can trigger comment-triggered automation (Atlantis, issue_comment workflows).

facts.behavior: Connects claude.ai/code or the Claude mobile app to a Claude Code session running on your machine; 'Claude keeps running locally the entire time', so filesystem, local MCP servers, tools and project config stay available (hooks and settings are the local ones). Modes: `claude remote-control` (server mode), `claude --remote-control`/--rc (interactive), `/remote-control`//rc in a session (carries history), VS Code, Desktop. Connection is outbound HTTPS only, no inbound ports; transcript is stored on Anthropic servers while connected. Auto-reconnects after sleep or network drop.
facts.limits: Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise; no API keys; Team/Enterprise Owner must enable. Unavailable on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, non-api.anthropic.com ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, Claude apps gateway, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC or DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK; not for ZDR/HIPAA orgs. Local process must keep running (close terminal = offline). One remote session per interactive process; server mode default capacity 32 (--capacity), spawn modes same-dir/worktree/session. Server mode gives up after ~10 minutes network outage; interactive 403s retried up to 3 minutes, heartbeat failure disconnects after ~30 minutes. Server mode --sandbox/--no-sandbox removed v2.1.300; global flags like --settings are not carried over (refuses to start). Terminal-only commands (/plugin, /resume) work only locally. Forwarded non-permission dialogs expire after 5 minutes by default (dialogExpiry). Resume after stopping server works about 4 hours. disableRemoteControl setting turns it off; remoteControlAtStartup=true honored only in user/managed settings, project-level true ignored.

facts.feature: Remote Control Trusted Devices and mobile push
facts.behavior: Optional org setting 'Require trusted devices': each device enrolls a credential and sign-in must be under 18 hours old (biometric/passkey step-up). Mobile push notifications while Remote Control is active: Claude decides when to push (task finished, decision needed) or on request; two /config toggles (Push when Claude decides, Push when actions required).
facts.limits: Trusted Devices applies only to sessions started after enabling; no per-team scoping. No per-event push configuration beyond the two toggles. Push skipped while you focus the terminal (CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE can extend).

facts.feature: GitHub Actions: claude-code-action modes and triggers
facts.behavior: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 runs Claude Code inside workflows. Interactive mode (no prompt input) responds to the @claude trigger phrase; automation mode (prompt input given) runs on any event incl. cron schedule. prompt can be a skill invocation; repo skills need actions/checkout first. Before run, checks: triggering user must have write access (issue/PR events; allowed_non_write_users overrides, no-user events like schedule skip) and bot actors are rejected unless listed in allowed_bots (also applies to scheduled runs).
facts.limits: In automation mode results go to the workflow run log unless the prompt directs posting and a posting tool is allowed. With a plain-text prompt Claude has 'no shell or GitHub API access until you grant the tools' via --allowedTools in claude_args or permissions.allow in the settings input; a skill's allowed-tools frontmatter grants its tools. Inline-comment MCP server starts only if --allowedTools in claude_args names it. GitHub runs scheduled workflows only from the default branch and disables schedules in public repos after 60 days without activity. Fork PRs get no secrets on public repos. GitHub does not trigger workflows on commits made with default GITHUB_TOKEN.

facts.feature: GitHub Actions: turn cap, timeout, cost controls
facts.behavior: 'Set --max-turns in claude_args to limit iterations'; 'Set workflow-level timeouts to avoid runaway jobs'; 'Use GitHub's concurrency controls to limit parallel runs'. claude_args accepts any CLI argument (--max-turns, --model, --mcp-config, --allowedTools, --debug). Without --model the action uses the Claude Code default model. Runs consume GitHub Actions minutes plus API tokens (or subscription with OAuth token).
facts.limits: The page documents NO default value for --max-turns and NO default action timeout; both are opt-in and listed under cost-management best practices, not as built-in guards. Timeouts and concurrency are GitHub features, not Claude Code ones.

facts.feature: GitHub Actions: setup, auth and permissions
facts.behavior: /install-github-app (github.com repos only; needs gh CLI and repo admin) installs the Claude GitHub App, stores ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN as a repo secret, and opens a workflow PR. Manual setup possible. Org rollout via org-level app install, org secrets, reusable workflow; OIDC workload identity federation inputs avoid static secrets; Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry via use_bedrock/use_vertex/use_foundry with OIDC. The shared GitHub App requests a broad permission set (Actions r/w, Checks r/w, Contents r/w, Discussions, Issues, PRs, Repository hooks, Workflows r/w, etc.); action itself relies on Contents, Issues, Pull requests.
facts.limits: GitHub does not allow accepting a subset of app permissions; a custom GitHub App is needed for least privilege and covers only the Action (not Code Review or web auto-fix). OAuth token is tied to one person's subscription, so use API key for org-shared secrets. Never commit keys. CLAUDE.md in the repo is read on every run.

unreachable: No assigned page was unreachable. Remote Control, Monitor (tools-reference) and cloud-environments pages were read from saved fetch output after truncation; the middle of the Remote Control Trusted Devices section and a few later table rows were cut off by the fetch tool and not read in full. Pages beyond the five assigned (tools-reference.md, cloud-environments.md) were fetched additionally to cover Monitor and cloud reach. Not fetched: desktop-scheduled-tasks, settings (settings-in-cloud-sessions), claude-projects, self-hosted-environments, and the claude-code-action repo docs (security.md, usage.md), so per-action default max-turns/timeouts in the action's own inputs table are unconfirmed.

area: cost, context and model configuration (Claude Code docs, fetched 2026-10-21)

facts.behavior: "The Session block at the top of /usage shows detailed token usage statistics for your current session. Claude Code computes the dollar figure locally from token counts at list price, unless a modelPricing table is in effect." Totals reset on /clear (since v2.1.211). Figure is an estimate; authoritative billing is the Console Usage page. Docs name /usage, not /cost; /cost is not described on the costs page.
facts.limits: Estimate only; not billing. Session block aimed at API users (subscribers see plan bars). Plan breakdown is computed from local session history on this machine only; excludes other devices and claude.ai. Does not block or warn on spend.

facts.behavior: After the first main-conversation response, adds a line with request count, share of input tokens from cache, misses (with likely cause, v2.1.260+), expected rebuilds (compaction or tool-result clearing), and warm/cold with TTL in effect. Requires v2.1.251+. Status line scripts can read the same via the prompt_cache object.
facts.limits: Main conversation only, not subagents. /clear resets it. Informational.

facts.feature: /usage plan breakdown, recommendations, and f fix shortcut
facts.behavior: On Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, /usage shows attribution to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, loops, and recommendations for behaviors behind 10%+ of recent usage (e.g. trim CLAUDE.md, switch effort, compact before stepping away). Pressing f (v2.1.305+) runs rows ending in an /effort command and gives Claude a prompt for other actionable rows; rows ending in "run /compact" do nothing on f.
facts.limits: Approximate; local history only. No f hint while Remote Control connected. Not shown for API-key users as plan data.

facts.behavior: Live approximate count of output tokens the current turn has produced (includes thinking and foreground subagent output).
facts.limits: Excludes input/context; resets each turn and on compaction; hidden when narrow or in screen reader mode; does not match /usage totals.

facts.behavior: "run /context for a live breakdown by category with optimization suggestions, including which CLAUDE.md and auto memory files loaded." Also "show what is currently consuming context" and shows MCP overhead.
facts.limits: Informational snapshot of the current session; does not alter context. Detailed page for /context not fetched.

facts.behavior: "/compact Focus on code samples and API usage" steers the summary. CLAUDE.md may carry a "# Compact instructions" section. Manual compact reads the whole conversation so on a large context is itself a large request; while cache is warm it reads the prefix from cache; after a gap longer than the TTL it reprocesses uncached.
facts.limits: Replaces history with a summary (invalidates conversation-layer cache). DISABLE_COMPACT=1 disables both auto compaction and /compact.

facts.behavior: Re-injected from disk: system prompt/output style, project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules, auto memory, plan-mode plan; skill descriptions rebuilt (v2.1.304+). Up to five most recently modified read/edited files re-read (files over 5,000 tokens come back as path reference only). Invoked skill bodies re-injected, capped 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 total, oldest dropped first. Rules with paths: frontmatter and nested CLAUDE.md are reloaded on demand, not guaranteed. "Context that hooks added earlier" is summarized with the rest. SessionStart hooks matching source compact run again and their output is added.
facts.limits: Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md that loaded into message history are summarized away; docs advise dropping paths: frontmatter or moving to root CLAUDE.md if must persist. Skill truncation keeps start of file.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code compacts automatically as you approach the limit." Default: compacts when conversation reaches the model's context limit, except: Sonnet 4.6/Opus 4.6 without extended context compact at 200K; native-1M models (Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.7+) compact at about 967K tokens by default; with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 native-1M models compact at 200K; cloud sessions compact near the model limit; unrecognized model IDs compact at an assumed window.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1 skips proactive compaction for unrecognized IDs. Raising CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS reduces effective window before auto-compaction.

facts.feature: Auto-compact window controls (/autocompact, --autocompact, autoCompactWindow, modelSettings, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE, DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT)
facts.behavior: Window size 100K to 1M tokens, capped at model window. Precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (env) overrides command, flag, and autoCompactWindow setting; /autocompact saves per model under modelSettings (v2.1.288+); --autocompact is one-launch. CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE sets 1-100 percent of the window, can only lower, applies to main and subagents. DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 disables automatic and idle compaction (manual /compact stays) and overrides autoCompactEnabled setting.
facts.limits: Env var bare number 200 means 200 tokens (ignored/invalid) whereas /autocompact 200 means 200,000; suffixed values like 200k need v2.1.304+. Status line used_percentage measures against full window not the override.

facts.behavior: "compacts a long conversation that you've stepped away from, shortly before its prompt cache expires." On by default when ALL hold: interactive terminal session; conversation on the one-hour cache TTL; Claude Code can fetch feature flags from Anthropic; context reached threshold (default 200,000 tokens); about 54 minutes since the last request and computer awake. Shows 'Compacted while idle, before the prompt cache expired'. Fires PreCompact/PostCompact with matcher auto. Off via idleCompaction:false (v2.1.290+), /config row (v2.1.302+), or DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1. Threshold via CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS (floor 100000).
facts.limits: Not in -p/headless or non-terminal sessions; not on 5-minute TTL (API key, cloud provider, or subscription over plan usage); not without feature-flag fetch. Does not fire if computer asleep.

facts.behavior: Changelog 2.1.304: "Added a warning on Pro and Max plans when resuming an inactive conversation would use a noticeable share of your 5-hour usage limit: resume anyway, or start a new conversation and Claude can look up the previous one if you refer to it."
facts.limits: Only Pro and Max plans per changelog; no threshold, setting, or env var to configure it was found in the fetched pages; API-key, Team/Enterprise, and cloud-provider behavior not documented. Dedicated docs page for it not found (sessions page has no mention). Docs also note /compact is costliest on resuming an old session because the cache expired.

facts.feature: Prompt caching (automatic) and what invalidates it
facts.behavior: "Claude Code handles prompt caching for you, unless you disable it." Invalidating: switching models (each model has its own cache), changing effort on most models (not Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5/Haiku 5.5/Fable 5.1 on API key or subscription), turning on fast mode first time, connecting/removing MCP servers when tools are not deferred, deny of an entire tool when tool search off, compaction, image batch removal, upgrading Claude Code. Keeps cache: editing repo files, editing CLAUDE.md mid-session (but edit does not apply until /clear, /compact, or restart), permission mode changes, output style change (delivered as a conversation message), skills/commands, /recap, /rewind, subagent spawn.
facts.limits: Cache is effectively scoped to one machine and directory. Behind a gateway, caching depends on gateway handling of cache_control.

facts.feature: Prompt cache TTL defaults and controls
facts.behavior: Two buckets: main conversation, and everything else (subagents, workflows, teammates, forks, compaction, session titles). Default: one hour for main conversation only on a Claude subscription within plan usage; otherwise five minutes (API key, cloud provider, usage credits). Controls accept only 5m or 1h: promptCacheTtl setting / CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL (main); subagentPromptCacheTtl / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL (everything else); all need v2.1.242+. Precedence: FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 (forces 5m both buckets) > bucket env var > bucket setting > subagent frontmatter experimental cacheTtl (v2.1.248+) > ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 (requests 1h both buckets) > default.
facts.limits: 1-hour writes billed at a higher rate. 1h TTL not available through Claude apps gateway; gateway must forward anthropic-beta header. Subagents get 5 minutes even on subscription unless set. ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H_BEDROCK deprecated. Managed settings env can set org policy.

facts.behavior: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 disables for all models and takes precedence; _HAIKU, _SONNET, _OPUS apply to the model the alias resolves to; _FABLE for Fable models only.
facts.limits: Per-model variants do not cover a model ID set explicitly that differs from what the alias resolves to. Documented as debugging aid: "For normal use, leave caching enabled."

facts.behavior: Priority: (1) /model during session, (2) claude --model, (3) ANTHROPIC_MODEL, (4) model field in settings, (5) ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL (v2.1.236+). /model Enter saves as default in user settings; s switches for this session only. --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL apply only to the launched session. In -p, /model applies to session only (v2.1.205+). Switch also reaches subagents that inherit the main model.
facts.limits: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL ignored when set to default/inherit/opusplan/haiku, when enforceAvailableModels on, or org restrictions exclude it. A resumed session continues on its saved model except where ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL applies.

facts.behavior: default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan ("uses opus during plan mode, then switches to sonnet for execution"). On the Anthropic API opus=Opus 5.5, sonnet=Sonnet 5.5, haiku=Haiku 5.5, fable=Fable 5.1. ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU,FABLE}_MODEL repin aliases.
facts.limits: Each opusplan plan-mode toggle is a model switch and starts a fresh cache. ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL deprecated.

facts.feature: Model-switch cache confirmation and PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch hooks
facts.behavior: /model at the terminal asks to confirm only while cache is warm and new model differs from last responder (v2.1.238+ checks TTL). PreModelSwitch (v2.1.251+) can block (exit 2 / decision block), allow (skips confirmation), deny, or ask; precedence deny > ask > allow; timeout blocks the switch (30s default). Runs for /model, Option+P picker, /config model, fast mode that changes model, SDK/Remote Control set_model. PostModelSwitch delivers additionalContext with the next request.
facts.limits: PreModelSwitch does NOT run for automatic model fallback or model restore on resume (PostModelSwitch only). "ask" works only for /model in an interactive session; in -p, /config, set_model it is treated as refusal. Hook cannot return updatedInput or additionalContext.

facts.behavior: Changelog 2.1.301: a conversation too long for the new model is summarized by the previous model first.
facts.limits: Only the changelog entry was read; details not in model-config page.

facts.behavior: Levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max for Fable 5.x, Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7, Sonnet 5.5/5, Haiku 5.5; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 lack xhigh. Unsupported level falls back to highest supported at or below. Resolution: explicit (CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, --effort, /effort) > settings (per-model modelSettings, then effortLevel) > model default (high; Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 default medium; Opus 4.7 xhigh). Enter in slider saves default; s applies to session only (v2.1.257+). max applies to current session only unless set by CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; max not accepted in effortLevel or per-model setting.
facts.limits: Skill/subagent frontmatter effort overrides session level but not the env var. maxEffortLevel (managed) caps effort; picker hides levels above cap and naming a higher level runs at the cap; lower cap wins. effortLevel and env var do not accept ultracode. Changing effort mid-session invalidates cache on most models and asks to confirm while warm. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL accepts auto.

facts.behavior: modelSettings keyed by model ID, each entry may hold effortLevel, maxEffortLevel, autoCompactWindow (100000-1000000 or "auto", v2.1.288+); model entry beats top-level key in same file. maxEffortLevel can cap every model or per model on every provider. effortLevel is the default for models without a saved level.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL and --effort override both. maxEffortLevel cap still applies over the env var.

facts.behavior: "a high-speed configuration for Claude Opus, making the model up to 2.5x faster at a higher cost per token." Supported on Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8 only (not Sonnet, Haiku, Opus 4.7). Pricing per MTok input/output $8/$40 Opus 5.5; $10/$50 Opus 5 and 4.8. Persists across sessions by default; fastModePerSessionOptIn true starts each session off. Enabling on an unsupported model switches model to Opus. Enabling adds a request header in the cache key, so first request is fully uncached (once per conversation). Rate limit falls back to standard speed with cooldown.
facts.limits: Anthropic API / subscription only (not Bedrock, Vertex/Agent Platform, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS). Subscriptions need usage credits (billed from credits, not plan limits). Team/Enterprise disabled by default until Owner enables. Managed fastMode:false or fastModePerSessionOptIn or availableModels excluding Opus can refuse /fast. In -p, /fast works only if launched with fastMode in --settings (v2.1.205+). CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FAST_MODE=1 disables. Research preview.

facts.behavior: Env var naming the model setting for a session; priority 3 below --model and /model, above settings model. Applies only to the session launched with it; on next launch Claude Code returns to the variable's model regardless of a /model save.
facts.limits: Blocked by availableModels (replaced at startup with a warning, session starts on default model).

facts.behavior: "The default model for subagents, agent team teammates, and workflow agents that aren't assigned a model another way. Accepts an alias such as haiku or a full model name. A per-invocation model or a definition's model field, including inherit, takes precedence." Subagent resolution order: (1) per-invocation model parameter, (2) definition model frontmatter (inherit = main model), (3) CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, (4) main conversation's model. Before v2.1.251 the env var came first and overrode everything.
facts.limits: Alone, does not change built-in Explore and Plan subagents. Set to inherit equals unset. Checked against availableModels: blocked family alias runs newest permitted version, other blocked values fall back to inherited model. Subagents inherit thinking setting; no per-subagent thinking setting.

facts.behavior: Set to 1 (v2.1.257+) to force one model onto every subagent, teammate, and workflow agent. With both vars set, subagents run on CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL. While on, "Claude Code ignores the model field in subagent definitions, and Claude can't pass a model when starting a subagent." Verify with /tasks.
facts.limits: With FORCE alone, subagents use the main conversation's model, except built-in Explore which runs on its listed model. Forks and skills in a subagent with model: inherit still run on the main model. This is the only _FORCE variant for models; FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M is the other FORCE var (cache TTL).

facts.behavior: Managed/policy allowlist of selectable models (family, version prefix, or full ID). When managed defines it, that list alone applies (user/project cannot extend). /model rejects blocked switch with error; --model/ANTHROPIC_MODEL/model replaced at startup with a warning. area: Sandbox filesystem and network policy, output styles, statusline, OpenTelemetry monitoring (Claude Code docs as of 2026-10-21; changelog top is 2.1.306)

facts.behavior: "The sandbox covers shell commands only. Claude's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks run outside it." Limits apply to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and the processes they start. Off by default (enable with /sandbox or sandbox.enabled). Runs on macOS (Seatbelt), Linux and WSL2 (bubblewrap + socat). Subagents run in the same process and use the parent's sandbox config; background sessions are sandboxed when their settings enable it.
facts.limits: On native Windows commands run unsandboxed. Not covered: built-in Read/Edit/Write/WebFetch/WebSearch (follow permission rules), command hooks, local MCP servers, plugin monitors, LSP servers, helper commands such as the statusLine command and apiKeyHelper (all 'run with your full access'), processes started by mods, computer use. Commands typed at the ! shell-mode prompt run unsandboxed in most sessions (strict mode sandboxes them only in background sessions and Linux sessions with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB set).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (What runs outside the sandbox; Scope; Get started)

facts.behavior: "By default, if the sandbox can't start because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported, Claude Code runs commands without sandboxing." Setting failIfUnavailable true makes Claude Code exit at startup instead.
facts.limits: Default is silent fallback to unsandboxed execution. On native Windows with the flag set, Claude Code exits at startup. Boolean keys set in managed settings override developer-local values.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Get started warning; Enforce sandboxing with managed settings)

facts.behavior: Writes: working directory, per-user temp dir, and added directories (--add-dir, /add-dir, permissions.additionalDirectories). Reads: "most of the machine, including credential files such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials". Enforced at OS level for all child processes. filesystem arrays (allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead, allowRead) merge across settings scopes.
facts.limits: Default read policy exposes credential files. Sandbox paths use standard conventions (/abs, ~/rel), unlike Read/Edit permission rules (//abs, /path project-relative). In a linked git worktree, writes to the main repo's shared .git are allowed except hooks/ and config.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (What the sandbox restricts; Configure sandboxing; Filesystem isolation)

facts.behavior: "A denyRead entry doesn't stop the Read tool, and allowedDomains doesn't limit WebFetch." Settings reference: denyRead "Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths"; default unset. Paths from sandbox settings and from Read/Edit permission rules are merged into the final sandbox config (a Read deny rule feeds the sandbox, but a sandbox denyRead does not feed the Read tool).
facts.limits: Applies only to sandboxed Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands. To block Claude's Read tool use a Read(...) deny permission rule. A denyRead is not enforced when sandbox.filesystem.disabled is true. Narrower rule wins on overlap; an exact or wildcard denyRead holds inside a broader allowRead. permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is a separate switch that denies sandboxed commands reads of home dirs and mounted volumes.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (What runs outside the sandbox; Configure sandboxing; Permission rules); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md (sandbox.filesystem.denyRead)

facts.behavior: Declares credential files and env vars to protect from sandboxed commands. File entries with mode deny get the same read block as filesystem.denyRead; envVars with deny are unset before each sandboxed command. mode mask shows a per-session sentinel and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to allowed hosts (injectHosts); on macOS a masked file is simply unreadable. deny entries merge from all scopes; no scope can remove another's deny. deny beats mask.
facts.limits: "There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted." Affects sandboxed Bash commands only; to strip credentials from all subprocesses use CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB. File deny does not apply if filesystem isolation is disabled (env var deny/mask still does; macOS file mask still holds). mask needs network.tlsTerminate and is honored only from user, managed, --settings (ignored in repo settings); mask falls back to deny for directories, globs, files over 8 MiB, non-UTF-8. Default onExtractNoMatch=warn can leave the real file readable. Env vars are otherwise inherited by sandboxed commands including secrets.

facts.behavior: Turns off filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Default false. Requires v2.1.216+. Honored only from user settings, managed settings, --settings; project settings cannot set it. If managed settings configure sandbox.filesystem or any credentials.files deny entry, only managed settings can set it. Ignored from every source when CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB is set.
facts.limits: With it on, denyRead and credentials.files deny are not enforced; commands can write shell startup files, PATH executables, ~/.claude/settings.json. autoAllowBashIfSandboxed still defaults true.

facts.behavior: Sandbox denies writes inside otherwise writable dirs to: .claude settings files and .claude/skills, agents, commands, hooks, .mcp.json, .claude/workflows, scheduled_tasks.json (cwd and parents); in cwd: .bashrc/.zshrc, .gitconfig, .vscode, .idea, .git/hooks and .git/config; bare-repo markers (HEAD, objects, refs); and most of ~/.claude plus ~/.claude.json and .credentials.json.
facts.limits: "There is no way to exempt one of these paths": allowWrite or an Edit allow rule does not lift it; only filesystem.disabled does. Distinct from permission-system protected paths. Applies to sandboxed commands only, not to the Edit/Write tools.

facts.feature: Sandbox network policy: allowedDomains / deniedDomains / proxy
facts.behavior: Sandboxed commands have no direct route out (separate network namespace on Linux/WSL2; Seatbelt on macOS). Traffic goes through a local proxy that checks each hostname against allowedDomains (starts empty) and deniedDomains; an entry with no port allows every port. Unlisted hosts: bypassPermissions allows, manual/acceptEdits prompts, auto mode refuses unless the command listed the host and the classifier approved, dontAsk refuses. deniedDomains blocks in every mode and beats wildcard allows. Proxy also refuses allowed hostnames resolving only to loopback/link-local/own-machine addresses. WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules are also merged into the sandbox allowlist.
facts.limits: "allowedDomains doesn't limit WebFetch" (WebFetch follows permission rules; WebSearch likewise). Filters by client-supplied hostname and by default does not inspect TLS, so domain fronting is possible; broad domains like github.com can enable exfiltration. Tools that ignore proxy env vars (plain ssh, most DB drivers) and non-TCP (UDP, QUIC, ping) cannot connect even to allowed hosts. Linux: localhost is private to the command; macOS needs allowLocalBinding. git over SSH fails on macOS. Setting httpProxyPort/socksProxyPort bypasses Claude Code's own domain controls (your proxy must filter).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Network isolation; Hosts outside your allowed domains; Security limitations; Custom proxy configuration)

facts.behavior: strictAllowlist true (user, managed, or --settings only; v2.1.219+) denies sandboxed commands any host outside the allowlist instead of prompting, in every permission mode. allowManagedDomainsOnly in managed settings blocks non-allowed domains automatically and honors only managed allowedDomains and WebFetch allow rules; also makes the sandbox admin-required and refuses per-command auto-mode host lists.
facts.limits: Sandboxed commands only; WebFetch still follows its permission rules. strictAllowlist in repo settings has no effect.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Network isolation; Per-command allowed domains in auto mode)

facts.feature: Per-command allowed domains in auto mode
facts.behavior: In auto mode with sandboxing on, each Bash/PowerShell/Monitor command can carry a list of hosts beyond the allowlist; the classifier reviews hosts with the command; approval opens those hosts for that one command only (v2.1.271+).
facts.limits: Nothing added to session allowlist or settings; deniedDomains still block; refused when strictAllowlist or allowManagedDomainsOnly locks the allowlist.

facts.behavior: Changelog 2.1.305: "Added sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces so sandboxed commands on Linux can create user namespaces (Chromium, rootless podman); this lets them get around the sandbox's file protections".
facts.limits: Not documented on the sandboxing page or in settings-reference.md (grep of the full settings reference found no entry; its sandbox object type list omits it). Only the changelog line is available: no default, scope or which settings files may set it is documented. By the changelog's own words, enabling it defeats the sandbox's file protections.

facts.behavior: Each weakens the sandbox. enableWeakerNestedSandbox lets the Linux sandbox run inside an unprivileged container (bind-mounts existing /proc). Developer user settings or --settings can turn them on, and so can repo .claude/settings.json unless the sandbox is admin-required (allowAppleEvents cannot be turned on from a repo). Set false in managed settings to prevent use.
facts.limits: Docs say enableWeakerNestedSandbox "considerably weakens security"; allowAppleEvents "removes code-execution isolation". No warning is emitted at use. Under an admin-required sandbox a repo's true values for the first four are ignored.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Keep developers from widening the policy; Security limitations; Troubleshooting)

facts.behavior: Auto-allow mode (default when enabled, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed true) approves sandboxed commands without prompt; regular-permissions mode keeps normal prompts. Claude may retry a failed command with dangerouslyDisableSandbox; approval depends on permission mode (bypassPermissions no prompt, manual/acceptEdits prompt, auto mode classifier, dontAsk denies). A matching allow rule such as Bash(curl *) also approves the retry. allowUnsandboxedCommands:false (strict sandbox mode) makes Claude Code ignore the parameter.
facts.limits: Auto-allow still honors Bash deny rules, content-scoped ask rules, critical-path rm. excludedCommands run fully unsandboxed (patterns match call text; script or make calling docker internally does not match). Strict mode sandboxes commands Claude runs, not ! commands (except noted sessions).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Sandbox modes; The unsandboxed retry escape hatch; excludedCommands)

facts.behavior: Sandbox becomes admin-required when managed settings (or --settings) set allowUnsandboxedCommands false, or managed settings set allowManagedDomainsOnly true (v2.1.285+). Then Claude Code ignores loosening keys in a repo's .claude/settings.json and settings.local.json (excludedCommands, allowedDomains, allowWrite, Edit allow rules for sandbox purposes, additionalDirectories, proxy ports, weaker-sandbox true values). allowManagedReadPathsOnly restricts allowRead to managed entries. Boolean keys set in managed settings override local values; array keys merge unless locked.
facts.limits: Does not turn the sandbox on (set enabled too). Developer ~/.claude/settings.json can still add most loosening entries; most have no managed-only lock. Claude's file tools still follow repo Edit rules and additional directories.

facts.feature: Output styles: what they are and how they alter the prompt
facts.behavior: "An output style is a set of instructions that sets Claude's role, tone, and response format for every response in a session." Claude Code sends the active style's instructions with every request. Built-ins: Default (no style), Proactive, Concise (v2.1.237+), Explanatory, Learning; the non-default built-ins keep the standard software-engineering instructions and add their own. Custom styles on the full system prompt omit Claude Code's built-in software engineering instruction section unless frontmatter keep-coding-instructions: true.
facts.limits: "An output style gives Claude instructions to follow. It doesn't guarantee that something always happens or never happens." "nothing enforces it". keep-coding-instructions has no effect on the shorter system prompt (set CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0 for full). Applies to main conversation and forks; other subagents run their own system prompt, so styles do not change them. Does not change permission mode (Proactive does not alter permission prompts). Docs point to hooks for must-happen behavior and CLAUDE.md for project knowledge. Adds input tokens; mid-session switch applies from next message (cache cost).

facts.feature: Output style configuration, locations and frontmatter
facts.behavior: Select via /output-style <style> (also works in non-interactive and Agent SDK sessions), /config menu, VS Code menu, or settings key outputStyle (case-sensitive built-in names; a non-matching value silently gives Default). Custom style files: ~/.claude/output-styles, .claude/output-styles (loaded from every dir between cwd and repo root, closest wins), managed-policy .claude/output-styles. Plugins can ship output-styles/. Frontmatter: name, description, keep-coding-instructions (default false), force-for-plugin (plugin styles only; applies automatically when plugin enabled, overrides user outputStyle). Command saves choice to .claude/settings.local.json.
facts.limits: Misspelled frontmatter fields are ignored without error; unparseable YAML loads style with no fields (see claude --debug). Terminal reads style files at startup, so edits need a restart. Remote Control surfaces list only built-in styles. A Proactive style 'check with you before deleting data' is an instruction, separate from permission prompts.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/output-styles (Change your output style; Create a custom output style; Frontmatter reference)

facts.behavior: statusLine setting (user or project settings): type "command", command (script path or inline shell), optional padding (default 0), refreshInterval (seconds, min 1), hideVimModeIndicator. Claude Code pipes JSON session data on stdin and displays stdout. Runs at session start/resume, then after new assistant message, /compact, permission-mode change, vim toggle, command change, refreshInterval, rate-limit resets_at, or prompt-cache expires_at; debounced 300ms; an in-flight script is cancelled when a new update fires. Supports multi-line, ANSI colors, OSC 8 links; COLUMNS and LINES env vars set. /statusline generates a script from natural language. Runs locally, consumes no API tokens. Companion subagentStatusLine setting customizes subagent panel rows.
facts.limits: Output shown only if script exits 0 with output; non-zero or empty output leaves the line blank. Stays blank until workspace trust is accepted (same rule as hooks in settings files). If disableAllHooks is true outside managed settings, only a managed statusLine runs, otherwise disabled; allowManagedHooksOnly gates apply. Hidden during help menu and permission prompts; shares a row with notifications outside fullscreen. Replaces most footer keyboard hints. The sandboxing page lists the statusline command as running outside the sandbox with full access. Docs do not state whether it runs in headless (-p) mode (not addressed; it is a UI element). It is display-only and cannot block or alter anything.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline (How status lines work; Troubleshooting; Subagent status lines); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (What runs outside the sandbox)

facts.behavior: Telemetry is off by default; CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 required. Signals: metrics (OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER: otlp/prometheus/console/none), logs/events (OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER), traces (beta; also needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER). OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL has no default and must be set. Defaults: metrics interval 60000ms, logs 5000ms, traces 5000ms, delta temporality. Works identically in -p and Agent SDK sessions. mTLS supported.
facts.limits: Observability only; does not block or alter tool calls. "Claude Code does not pass OTEL_* variables to subprocesses (Bash tool, hooks, MCP servers, language servers)." Hook execution is recorded only as the claude_code.hook span, which requires detailed beta tracing (ENABLE_BETA_TRACING_DETAILED=1 plus BETA_TRACING_ENDPOINT; interactive CLI needs org allowlist). internal_error not emitted on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or with DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING.

facts.behavior: Metrics: claude_code.session.count, lines_of_code.count, pull_request.count, commit.count, cost.usage, token.usage, code_edit_tool.decision, active_time.total. Events: user_prompt, assistant_response, tool_result, tool_decision (decision, source config/hook/user_*, tool_source builtin/mcp, classifier_verdict v2.1.301+), api_request, api_error, api_refusal, api_request_body/api_response_body, permission_mode_changed, auth, mcp_server_connection, internal_error, plugin_installed, plugin_loaded, managed_settings_resolved. prompt.id ties events from one prompt; event.sequence orders them. Attribution via query_source (main/subagent/auxiliary), agent.name, skill.name, mcp_server.name, mcp_tool.name; workflow.run_id on workflow-spawned agents.
facts.limits: The fetch of the page was truncated before the final events (plugin_loaded, managed_settings_resolved) so their fields are not captured. Telemetry records decisions and results, it does not enforce them. tool_result is not emitted for rejected calls. Hook runs are not logged as events. Custom/third-party plugin, skill and MCP names appear as custom/third-party/mcp unless OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1.

facts.feature: OpenTelemetry privacy controls and always-on attributes
facts.behavior: Content is redacted/off by default; opt-in flags: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1, OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 (bash commands, MCP/skill names, file paths, tool input, error text), OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 (tool output span events; requires tracing), OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES (entire conversation history; implies consent to the other flags), OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS. Content limit CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH default 61440. Cardinality toggles OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID/ACCOUNT_UUID (default true), VERSION/ENTRYPOINT/REPOSITORY (default false). OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES adds custom keys to all metrics and events.
facts.limits: user.id and user.email (when available) and terminal.type are always included; no documented option to exclude them. Extended-thinking content is redacted in raw bodies. Custom resource-attribute values cannot contain spaces.

facts.behavior: Admins set OTEL env vars in the managed settings env block. Claude Code ignores OTEL exporter variables in a repo's .claude/settings.json and settings.local.json, so a repo cannot enable telemetry, pick a destination or capture content; a repo can only disable a signal (exporter none) unless managed settings, --settings or the launching env set it. Managed OTLP endpoint/protocol/headers/cert remove developer-set per-signal values (and endpoints, for credentials). otelHeadersHelper (settings) emits JSON headers at startup and every 29 minutes (CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_HEADERS_HELPER_DEBOUNCE_MS), http/protobuf and http/json only. Helper failure stops exports and shows a once-per-session warning.
facts.limits: Exporter selectors (OTEL_*_EXPORTER) follow normal precedence (developer can disable a signal or switch to console) unless set in managed settings (v2.1.223+). Managed pinning "changes where telemetry is delivered, not what Claude Code collects". With grpc only static headers apply. Cloud sessions: collector domains must be on the network allowlist; do not put collector credentials in env vars.

facts.feature: OpenTelemetry traces, propagation, headless and subagents
facts.behavior: Beta spans: claude_code.interaction, llm_request, tool (with tool.blocked_on_user and tool.execution), hook (detailed beta only). Subagent spans nest under the parent Agent tool span with agent_id and parent_agent_id. Bash and PowerShell subprocesses inherit TRACEPARENT when tracing is active; model and HTTP MCP requests carry traceparent for the Anthropic API (CLAUDE_CODE_PROPAGATE_TRACEPARENT=1 for custom proxies). In Agent SDK and claude -p, inbound TRACEPARENT parents Claude's spans; events carry trace_id/span_id even without a traces exporter.
